clue.text: Boss given old-fashioned scarf to bind hair

parts.note: the boss is the head of an organisation
square is slang for conventional or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A manager is presented with a dated scarf for tying up their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A headsquare is a square of fabric folded and worn over the hair, a headscarf.

clue.text: In hospital department, most of film is clear

indicators.note: In tells us one piece sits inside the other, the shortened film placed within the department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

indicators.note: most of means the film word loses its final letter

parts.note: a video is a recorded film

explanation.surface: Something in a hospital ward, mostly footage, is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Ear, nose and throat is the hospital department crosswords use most; 'most of' drops the film word's last letter before 'In' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident and clear are synonyms, both meaning plainly seen or obvious.

clue.text: Cross over, making entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, especially in a church

explanation.surface: Crossing over to make a dramatic arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross over' reads as an action, but Cross is the noun ROOD, a church crucifix, and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is the usual way in to a room or building, an entrance.

clue.text: Tremble, seeing case for arrows

definitions.meaning: to tremble is to shake slightly, as with fear
an archer carries arrows in a ...

explanation.surface: Someone shakes at the sight of an archer's arrow holder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for shaking and the noun for an archer's arrow container.

clue.text: Lively arrangement for main date

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters of the words main date reorders them into a new word

explanation.surface: An exciting plan for the chief appointment in the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated and lively are synonyms describing someone full of energy and spirit.

clue.text: Standing up straight before court

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone stands tall before appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect describes something upright, held vertically rather than slouched.

clue.text: Be elected as MP for NW city? Or one in Hants?

parts.note: a candidate who is elected wins the seat
Chester is a city in north-west England

explanation.surface: A politician hoping to win a north-western seat, or perhaps a southern one.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county on the south coast whose historic city is Winchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city in question is the county town of Hampshire, so it is one city in Hants.

clue.text: African city's lapse leading to spillage of oil

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: leading to places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a trip is a slip or lapse

indicators.note: a spillage scatters the letters of oil into a new order

explanation.surface: A careless slip in a North African port causes an oil spill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, a city on the North African coast.

clue.text: Reportedly disposed of — from one end to the other!

definitions.text: from one end to the other

indicators.note: Reportedly says we hear a phrase spoken and enter the word it resembles

parts.note: to have disposed of something is to have thrown it out

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something was got rid of completely, end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means across the whole extent of something, from start to finish.

clue.text: Ancient British tribe's choice nickname? Not entirely

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: Not entirely signals that only part of the words choice nickname is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A tribe's preferred nickname, not fully told.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were the tribe of East Anglia led by Boudicca against Roman rule.

clue.text: Genuine-sounding Scottish dance

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for genuine is heard rather than written

parts.note: something genuine is real

explanation.surface: An authentic Highland dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The reel is a lively Scottish folk dance in which couples weave figures of eight.

clue.text: Nit-picking editor meeting worker in film

indicators.note: in puts the editor and worker inside the word for film

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A fussy editor meets a crew member on a movie set.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic describes someone overly concerned with minor details and rules, a nit-picker.

clue.text: Woman accommodating Scandinavians and Africans

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the Scandinavians go inside the woman's name

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name
Danes are people from Denmark, in Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A hostess puts up guests from Scandinavia and from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudanese people are natives of Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Regret following a French team at first? Not so

indicators.note: following places regret after the earlier pieces

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of team

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Regret after a French side starts badly, though perhaps that is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue describes a statement that is false, one that is not so.

clue.text: Extra supporter beside entrance to exhibition?

parts.note: a leg supports a table or body
by means next to or beside

indicators.note: entrance to picks the first letter of exhibition

explanation.surface: An additional support stand next to the way into a show.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a leg bye is a run scored off the batsman's body, counted as an extra rather than to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Extras are cricket runs not credited to a batsman, and leg byes are one kind.

clue.text: Titled man, one with little time to support pub

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the pub comes first

parts.note: a bar is a pub
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A nobleman and a friend with little time to spare prop up the local pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British title ranking below a baron, so he is a titled man.

clue.text: Wager involving everyone in dance company

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the word for everyone goes inside the wager

parts.note: a bet is a wager
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A bet that drags everyone into a dance troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet can be a company of classical dancers, such as the Royal Ballet.

clue.text: Scottish festival always associated with chap minding pigs?

parts.note: a hog man would be a man who tends hogs, or pigs
ay is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A festival forever linked with a pig keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish celebration of New Year's Eve.

clue.text: Easy elegance of good people

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Fine people show effortless poise.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is smooth, effortless elegance of movement or manner.

clue.text: Summons from major ultimately involved in intelligence

indicators.note: involved in places the final letter inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: wit means intelligence or quick thinking

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of major

explanation.surface: An order from an army major in military intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a written court order, such as one summoning someone to appear.

clue.text: Outdoor market of moderate quality

definitions.meaning: a gathering with stalls selling goods in the open

explanation.surface: An open-air market that is only so-so.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an open-air trading event and something middling, as in a fair performance.

clue.text: Employment America for example backed

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

indicators.note: backed means the abbreviation for for example is reversed

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: American jobs, for instance, supported by others.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the act of employing something, its use.

clue.text: Student, fifty, one bringing in money

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an earner brings in money

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old student who also holds down a paying job.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject, a student.

clue.text: Touring City, relate to wavering voters

indicators.note: Touring means going round, so the shuffled letters surround the City
wavering suggests unsteady movement, so the letters of relate to are rearranged

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Canvassers going round the City try to connect with undecided voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' with a capital is the City of London, whose postcode letters are the crossword standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote.
